scenes.narration: Three quarters of the animals in the deep ocean make their own light.
scenes.visual: dark ocean water, shafts of light fading into black

scenes.narration: Down there, sunlight never arrives. The last of it gives out around a thousand metres.
scenes.visual: a depth gauge descending past a thousand metres

scenes.narration: So they built their own. A chemical reaction in their skin, cold and blue, burning almost no energy.
scenes.visual: close-up of blue bioluminescence in dark water

scenes.narration: Some use it to hunt. Some use it to vanish, lighting their bellies to erase their shadow from below.
scenes.visual: a silhouetted fish seen from below against faint light

scenes.narration: The most common signal in the ocean is not a sound. It is a flash.
scenes.onScreen: The ocean's loudest signal is light
scenes.visual: a single bright flash in total darkness
